citation: Spangelo et al. (2013), Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) Applied to Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) CubeSat Mission Operational Scenarios
title: Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) Applied to Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) CubeSat Mission Operational Scenarios
venue_type: conference paper; venue name not stated in paper text (DOI metadata provided)
modeling_scope: System-level CubeSat/RAX mission MBSE for operational scenarios, including mission, flight system, ground system, environment, logical and physical subsystem models, requirements traceability, architecture, behavior, state machines, parametric analyses, communication link/SNR analysis, power/energy simulation, schedules, and verification/validation support. EPS coverage is through the Power Collection and Control subsystem, on-board energy state, solar energy collection, power consumption, battery energy limits, and schedule feasibility.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML with MagicDraw/No Magic Teamwork, Cameo Simulation Toolkit, ParaMagic, Systems Tool Kit (STK), PHX ModelCenter, MATLAB, Excel/Mathematica wrappers, a CubeSat-specific SysML extension/framework, and the Develop With What You Fly With philosophy.
robot_platform: RAX CubeSat/nanosatellite mission, including RAX-1 and RAX-2; paper describes CubeSats as standardized one-to-three-cube nanosatellites but does not state RAX's exact unit form factor in the extracted text.
task_domain: Space weather mission operations for studying ionospheric plasma field-aligned irregularities using a bi-static radar configuration; modeling covers orbit/attitude context, energy collection, science data acquisition, on-board data storage, downlink/uplink, ground station access, and operational scheduling.
interface: Tool/model integration interfaces among MagicDraw SysML models, CST, ParaMagic, STK, PHX ModelCenter, MATLAB, Excel/Mathematica; model repository/collaboration interfaces; flight-ground command and telemetry interface; subsystem interfaces among OBC, communications, payload, bus, ADCS, thermal, data handling, and power.
feedback: Model execution supports run-view-update loops: solved parametric values can be updated back to SysML, analyses can be automatically rerun with updated parameters, expected behavior can be compared with on-flight observed behavior, and future operations can update schedules/parameters with operational performance feedback.
control_autonomy_split: Ground operations generate command sets/schedules; the onboard computer processes uploaded commands and dispatches them to relevant subsystems near execution time. Broader autonomous control allocation is not discussed.
network_latency_assumptions: Ground station visibility, line-of-sight access, uplink/downlink states, and ground network parameters are modeled; no network latency assumptions are reported.
evaluation: Demonstrated as a RAX CubeSat case study by executing SysML parametric, state machine, and activity models. Examples include three ParaMagic communication SNR/link scenarios, a PHX ModelCenter power/energy/data workflow integrating STK and MATLAB, and CST behavior simulations of flight-ground and OBC/communications interactions. Formal validation against flight data is proposed as future work rather than completed.
rq_relevance: RQ1 partial: the paper gives a general CubeSat SysML framework/template and a RAX case including EPS/power functions, but it relies on RAX-specific mission behavior and does not frame the method as requiring minimal behavioral knowledge. RQ2 partial: it claims MBSE/model integration outcomes such as integrability, reuse, rapid scenario evaluation, robustness metrics, and requirements compliance, but does not measure reliability or reproducibility as EPS-specific outcomes. RQ3 partial: it links MBSE models to requirements compliance, V&V of software/interfaces, schedule/parameter verification, and a power scenario with violation metrics, but it does not present a dedicated EPS verification procedure prior to physical development.
claimed_outcomes: Integrated modeling environment enables automated flow of information between simulators, reducing manual information transfer and supporting rapid evaluation of design configurations and mission scenarios.
Users can extract feasibility, performance, and robustness metrics for representative mission scenarios.
Vehicle and network parameters and operational schedules can be verified before implementation, during operations, and updated with operational performance feedback.
The model can check requirements compliance and support trade studies through SysML parametric execution and PHX ModelCenter workflows.
A CubeSat model development kit/template is intended to help future teams describe, optimize, and evaluate their satellites and mission operations.
The modular approach enabled easy model growth and simultaneous contributions by multiple modelers; reusable components and tool integration support scalability.
No direct EPS reliability improvement or empirical reproducibility metric is reported. Robustness and integrability are claimed mainly for the MBSE/integrated simulation environment.
verification_validation_linkage: General V&V is explicit: SysML requirements can be traced to design, analysis, and verification elements; the model is said to verify design updates against mission requirements; ParaMagic/PHX workflows can verify requirements during design; CST supports verification and validation of the system; behavior simulations can compare expected and on-flight observed behavior and support V&V of mission software and interfaces. EPS-specific linkage is limited to the power scenario's energy/power simulation, requirements compliance checks, and violation outputs; no standalone EPS verification procedure is reported.
key_findings: The RAX SysML model decomposes the CubeSat mission into launch system, environment, mission, flight system, ground system, and operational/logical subsystems, with logical and physical models separated.

The power model represents solar energy acquisition, power distribution, excess energy storage in an on-board battery, power consumption, on-board energy state, and energy/data dynamics during operations.
The paper integrates SysML with CST, ParaMagic, STK, PHX ModelCenter, and MATLAB to execute parametric, state machine, and activity models for analysis and simulation.

The communication analysis uses a SysML parametric SNR/link model and demonstrates three causalities: compute SNR from power/rate, compute required power from SNR/rate, and compute achievable data rate from power/SNR.

The power scenario uses STK, SysML, MATLAB, and PHX ModelCenter to model dynamic orbits, solar collection opportunities, ground station access, on-board operations, data download, on-board energy, and data time histories.
The behavior analysis uses CST to simulate flight-ground, OBC command dispatch, and communication subsystem state transitions for upload, downlink, beacon, nominal, and experiment modes.
The paper states that interface behavior and information exchange can be tested, and expected behavior can be compared to on-flight observed behavior.

The authors report practical challenges with tool licensing, wrapper/integration setup, debugging wrapped MATLAB/STK models, prototype STK wrapping in ParaMagic, separate simulations, and the need for later flight-data validation.
limitations_gaps: Appropriate licenses are required for all simulation tools and vendor support was needed.
Creating and testing integration required wrapper files, wrapping models, saving, and reopening models in PHX ModelCenter and MagicDraw, making setup time consuming and inefficient.
Debugging MATLAB code and STK scenarios after wrapping into PHX ModelCenter was difficult, time consuming, and frustrating.
Wrapping STK models as parametric constraints and executing them using ParaMagic was only at a prototype stage.
Current simulations step through time for visualization; constraint-based solving with state constraints is identified as future work.
The simulations execute individually; integrating them for broader combined analyses, such as simultaneous power and communication optimization, is future work.
No unified environment for efficient verification of optimal scheduling algorithms was available; this is identified as a future need.
Comparison with real operational RAX data is proposed as future work to verify, validate, and improve the models.

quality.rationale: The paper has an IEEE DOI and conference-paper format, and it explicitly reports challenges, limitations, and future work. Venue name is not printed in the extracted paper text, but the provided DOI metadata supports a credible publication source.

notes_for_consistency: This is a supporting paper and extends a 2012 CubeSat MBSE paper cited by the authors. It is system-level with meaningful EPS/power modeling, but not an EPS-only paper. RQ2 outcomes are mostly integrability, robustness, reuse, and requirements-compliance claims from MBSE/model integration, not measured EPS reliability. RQ3 evidence is general V&V plus power-scenario requirements/violation checks, not a dedicated EPS verification-procedure model. Venue name is not explicit in paper.md; author spelling for Grant Soremekum/Soremekun differs between title metadata and biography, so metadata spelling is used.
